purpose: Adjudicated convention-C comparison sites for scripts/convention-c-value-audit.py. An entry here is the ONLY thing that stops a confirmed convention-C binding from blocking that audit.
why_a_committed_file: The audit reads no names and no comments, by design: its whole premise is that it cannot be evaded by re-spelling, and docs/audits/2026-08-15-detector-blindness-taxonomy.md records sixteen spellings that defeated shape-matching detectors, four of them found BY detectors written to catch the previous blind spot. A '# comparison only' comment or a z_C-style name would be an exemption an author grants themselves inside the file being audited -- the same evasion surface, one level up. A ledger entry cannot be granted that way. It lives outside the scanned tree, it must be committed as a separate deliberate act, and its key includes a hash of the site's own source line, so editing that line expires the adjudication automatically. Same shape as docs/audits/lean-vacuity-review-ledger.json, which holds agent verdicts a machine cannot reach for the same reason.
what_co_binding_is_not: The audit reports which confirmed-C sites are co-bound with a convention-D binding in the same enclosing scope. That is a value-level hint at which sites are PROBABLY comparisons, and it deliberately carries no exemption power: it can be gamed by adding a throwaway z_D beside the site. Co-binding is why a site gets PROPOSED for the ledger (--propose-ledger). It is never why a site is exempt; the commit is.
how_to_add_an_entry: 2. Take the stub for the site you are adjudicating.
3. Fill in `rationale` with why that site binds z_C deliberately -- what it compares, and what would be lost by binding only z_D.
5. Commit it here. Do NOT edit the audited source to make the site disappear; that is AGENTS.md 1a audit-dodging.

6. If the site's source line later changes, the entry stops matching and the site blocks again. That is intended: the adjudication was about that expression, and it is now a different one. The audit lists such entries as `stale` (non-blocking) so they can be pruned or renewed.

entries.rationale: `z_of(q, convention)` is a two-arm frame-comparison helper: the D arm returns the canonical `markov_z(q) = q**3/(q**2+1)`, the C arm returns `sqrt(q)/(q+1)`, and the probe calls both to measure the frame difference in the He-4 body-order shortfall. The function's own docstring scopes the C arm 'excised - computed here ONLY to measure the frame difference, never wired'. Binding only z_D would delete the comparison the probe exists to make. NOTE: --propose-ledger does NOT stub this site, because its D arm is a CALL (`markov_z(q)`) rather than an inline z_D binding, so the co-binding hint does not fire. Adjudicated by hand for that reason; see bean qou-1jny.
entries.adjudicated_by: claude (session 2b6a2d13)

entries.rationale: Deliberate convention-C retention, and the module says so at the site: "EXCISED -- audited here, not used". Its purpose is RECOGNITION, not computation: the weights the corpus once quoted are the ones z_C actually produces, so keeping this arm is what lets a reader identify a surviving C-era number wherever it turns up. Deleting it would remove that ability, which is the opposite of what excision is for. Note on why no pairing test finds this file's D arm: it is written in the parametrised fibre form z = q^N/[N]_q (equal to q^3/(q^2+1) at N=2), not the N=2 literal -- a third spelling beyond taxonomy rows 18 and 19.

entries.rationale: Two-arm C-vs-D comparison whose D arm lives in LEAN, not in this file. The probe's A5 assertion checks tr_C(pi_lambda) = w_lambda(t)*d_lambda against the Markov-forced weights of the Lean `BorromeanCanonicalTraceDerivation` (`trC_borromean_derived`), which is the convention-C arm of a deliberately-maintained C/D pair; the D arm is `BorromeanMarkovTrace`, and `BorromeanTraceConventionSplit.lean` proves D != C sorry-free. So z_C here is the object under comparison, not residual C: binding z_D would make the probe compare the D value against the Lean C weights and assert a known-false equality. RESOLVES the in-file note of 2026-08-10, which feared the reverse (that the Lean side had moved to D leaving this comparison mismatched). Evidence is the probe's own exact-symbolic PASS: because D != C is a THEOREM, a mismatched pairing could not pass, so the Lean weights it cites are necessarily C. Verified by running it (A5 traces: True, 4/4 assertions).

Two-arm frame-comparison helper `z_of(q, convention)`: the D arm returns the canonical `markov_z(q) = q**3/(q**2+1)`, the C arm returns `sqrt(q)/(q+1)`, and the probe evaluates BOTH to show its 2/3 threshold verdict is convention-independent. The function's own docstring scopes the C arm: 'excised, computed here ONLY to show the threshold verdict is convention-independent'. Binding only z_D would delete the comparison the probe exists to make -- the verdict's convention-independence is the result. Instance of taxonomy ROW 17 (the D arm is a CALL to the canonical helper, not an inline re-spelling, so the co-binding test sees no D-shaped expression in scope); same shape as the already-adjudicated he4_body_order_shortfall_location_probe.z_of, which is row 17's worked example.

This IS the sanctioned named convention-C source. `markov_parameter_convention_C` exists precisely so that a deliberate C consumer is greppable rather than inlining sqrt(q)/(1+q); flagging its own return as residual C would be flagging the guard for doing its job, and migrating it to z_D would make the function a liar to every caller that asks for C by name. The registry registers this symbol under `evaluators.z` as C so R9 asserts z_C numerically on every validator run. Newly VISIBLE (not newly introduced) on 2026-08-30: the helper was mpmath-only and raised TypeError on a sympy Symbol, so symbolic consumers had to inline C and were invisible to the guard (taxonomy row 21); adding the sympy branch is what put this return in the audit's view. The mpmath arm at the same site is the identical object in the other numeric tower.
